candidates.exact_span: The 4Q3 is 431.3 cubic feet per second (cfs) and the harmonic mean low flow used for human health calculations is 1108 cfs. To convert 4Q3 expressed in cfs to 4Q3 expressed as MGD, the constant 1.548 cfs/MGD is used. The 4Q3 is 278.6 MGD and the harmonic mean low flow is 715.8 MGD.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 4Q3 value (278.6 MGD) is an input to the critical dilution calculation that determines which TRC water quality standard governs the permit limit; different accepted flow values would change the derived limit and compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The NMWQS for total residual chlorine (TRC) are 11 ug/l for chronic and 19 ug/l for acute conditions. The NNWQS for TRC are 4000 ug/L for domestic water supply, and primary/secondary human contact; 19 ug/L for aquatic & wildlife habitat-acute; and, 11 ug/L for aquatic & wildlife habitat-chronic and livestock watering.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These are the underlying numeric standards used to derive and select the enforceable TRC limit; interpreting which standard category applies, or resolving the NMWQS/NNWQS labeling, would change the applicable numeric limit used for measurement comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Since acute conditions do not allow dilution; the limit must be met at end-of-pipe but chronic standards do allow dilution, the permit shall use the most stringent WQS for the permit limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether acute versus chronic treatment applies, and whether dilution may be credited, determines whether the end-of-pipe acute standard or a dilution-adjusted chronic standard governs; a different reading would change the selected enforceable limit.

candidates.exact_span:
Qe = facility effluent or design flow; 6.67 MGD
Qa = 4Q3; 278.6 MGD
F = fraction of stream allowed for mixing; 1.0
candidates.computation_change_reason: These are explicit inputs to the critical dilution formula; different interpretations of effluent flow, receiving-water flow, or mixing fraction would change CD and therefore the derived TRC limit.

The critical dilution formula structure determines how effluent and receiving-water flows combine; an alternative reading of the formula or variable definitions would change the calculated dilution factor and downstream limit selection.

candidates.exact_span:
The in-stream TRC concentration after allowing for dilution is; 11 ug/l ÷ 0.0234 = 470 ug/l.
Since this value is greater than the 19 ug/l end-of-pipe acute standard, the 19 ug/l is more stringent and will be more protective. The draft permit maintains the 19 ug/l end-of-pipe acute limit since it is more stringent and will be more protective than the 11 ug/l dilution based chronic limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage records the comparison that selects the operative 19 ug/l end-of-pipe limit over the dilution-based chronic alternative; if the arithmetic, stringency test, or selection rule were read differently, the applicable numeric limit for compliance would change.

candidates.exact_span: In addition to the 19 ug/l chemical specific limitation, the draft permit also maintains the narrative limit for total residual chlorine shall be "No Measurable." TRC shall be limited as follows: "After dechlorination and prior to final disposal, the effluent shall contain NO MEASURABLE (TRC) at any time. NO MEASURABLE will be defined as no detectable concentration of TRC as determined by any approved method established in 40 CFR Part 136.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The coexistence of a 19 ug/l numeric limit and a separate narrative no-detectable limit affects which enforceable standard applies to a given measurement and how non-detect or missing-result evidence is classified; different readings of whether both limits apply simultaneously would change limit comparison and missing-evidence semantics.

candidates.exact_span: The effluent limitation for TRC is the instantaneous maximum and cannot be averaged for reporting purposes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the limit is an instantaneous maximum with no averaging permitted changes how reported measurements are compared for compliance and what form of monitoring evidence is required to establish satisfaction of the limit.

candidates.exact_span: The maximum dechlorinated TRC shall be monitored daily by grab sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a daily grab-sample monitoring obligation for dechlorinated TRC; interpreting its scope, frequency, or trigger conditions differently would change whether monitoring was required on a given day or period.

candidates.exact_span: TRC shall be measured within fifteen (15) minutes of sampling.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required elapsed time between sampling and measurement affects whether a reported result counts as valid evidence of required monitoring and whether absent or late measurements should be treated as missing evidence versus satisfied obligations.

candidates.exact_span: After dechlorination and prior to final disposal, the effluent shall contain NO MEASURABLE (TRC) at any time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The temporal and process-stage scope ('after dechlorination', 'prior to final disposal', 'at any time') governs when the limit applies and when monitoring is expected; different interpretations of these conditions would change limit applicability, monitoring obligation windows, and how periods without data are classified.
